roles.trigger: Ledger, migration or export code changes.
roles.produced: docs/LEDGER_TRUNCATION_FINDING.md. This role was queued on a claim that turned out to be FALSE — "the RESTORE path is only described" — when proof:backup-restore has been exercising it on real Postgres in CI all along (16/16 live, including a flipped byte, a truncated archive and a missing manifest all REFUSED). The real gap was next to it: a hash chain detects EDITS, not deletions of its own tail. 40 records seeded on a live Postgres, the last 10 deleted with a plain DELETE, and db:verify-ledger printed "Chain intact" and exited 0. Pinned as an explicit assertion in proof:audit-ledger-pg (14/14), named in the threat model as its own Tampering row, documented in BACKUP_AND_RESTORE.md, and answered operationally with db:verify-ledger --min-records N — because the command already REFUSED a missing DATABASE_URL on the grounds that a verifier which green-lights the void is worse than none, and then exited 0 on an empty table.
roles.nextAction: SHIFT 2 (owner-sequenced, spec in the owner's words): build the database role split — the runtime role non-owner and minimally privileged (ledger: SELECT+INSERT only), schema/admin operations separate, and BOTH directions proven: legitimate ledger writes still work while destructive operations fail. The backup/restore proof must recreate the same privilege posture rather than accidentally restoring ownership (pg_restore --clean drops table-level grants with the objects). Does NOT reopen launch scope.

roles.title: DevEx / tooling engineer
roles.charter: The gate fabric itself — preflight, the proof harness, mutation guard, parity checks. Guards the guards.

Found and fixed one real hole: check-assist-conformance.mjs discovers TWO Assist clients (native/android/core Kotlin, native/desktop/core Rust) but ran only in desktop.yml, filtered to native/desktop/** and native/shared/**, so a change to the KOTLIN client never triggered the gate that binds it — the exact failure it exists to catch, in the client where it had already caught two real defects. Now runs in review-hub-ci.yml on every PR. Two other candidates were the false positive the parity gate already documents (npm alias vs script path), and check-ios-port-sources is correctly scoped since its subject lives entirely inside its filter
roles.nextAction: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 — the previous entry here asked for work already done a week earlier: it claimed check-preflight-ci-parity.mjs cannot resolve an npm alias against a script path, when aliasesFor/wired() have resolved exactly that since 43ec8f7, and LOCAL_ONLY is empty so there was no exemption to delete. The real open question is narrower and was found while checking that: wired() resolves aliases through a /scripts\/([a-z0-9-]+\.mjs)/ pattern, so a gate invoked through an npm script whose target is a .sh — or anything not .mjs — resolves to nothing and would read as unwired. Nothing is currently in that shape, which is why nobody has hit it. Either widen the pattern or state the limit in the file, so the next shell-script gate does not land on a silent false positive.

roles.title: Identity & Access domain lead
roles.charter: Entra, Okta, Keycloak, Ping, FIDO2. Owns 15 identity dimensions.
roles.trigger: An identity dimension changes, or its wire truth is unverified.
roles.produced: docs/IDENTITY_LIVE_SHAPE_CHECK.md — driven against a live Keycloak 26.4. Three fields sso-session names are NOT wire facts: amr is absent from the access token, the ID token, /userinfo and RFC 7662 introspection alike, leaving only an opaque deployment-configured acr, so single_factor/mfa/phishing_resistant is not derivable from a default IdP; auth_time is absent everywhere, so iat (token issuance) is not when the human authenticated — the same defect class as the RADIUS lastAuthAt finding; and the access token exp is 60s against a 36000s session max, demonstrated live at 75s with the token dead and four SSO sessions still alive. The session record carries no device field at all (id, username, userId, ipAddress, start, lastAccess, rememberMe, clients, transientUser), and two logins by the same user from the same host produced two indistinguishable sessions — precisely the leftover-session case the dimension exists for, so the device-session join must come from the device side. The code is already right (the connector normalizes a bridge-supplied value through oneOf with an unknown fallback and evaluate.ts raises the bar on every unknown); what was missing was the wire-truth record. proof:live-keycloak 14/14.
roles.nextAction: Ten of fifteen dimensions remain unverified against any live IdP, and only Keycloak was driven — Entra DOES emit amr and Okta exposes richer session APIs, so the wire-truth table is one IdP wide. Next: script the Keycloak client setup (KEYCLOAK_LIVE_INTEGRATION.md describes it in prose only, and following that prose cost this shift a 13/14 on a misread mapper value), then take passkey-assurance and token-binding against the same lab.

roles.title: Mac lane steward / local-lane operations
roles.charter: Owns the cloud side of the cloud↔Mac loop as a standing duty, not an ad-hoc errand: watches the remote for Mac pushes and branches, keeps lane-messages flowing both directions (nothing unread past one duty cycle, nothing sent without a committed push), tracks simulation-request debt (a pending request is REPORTED every cycle, never silently aged out), keeps the Mac's run instructions current when shared surfaces change, and escalates to the owner exactly the blockers only the owner can clear (auth, hardware, physical presence). Cannot operate the Mac itself — it is a separate machine with its own lane; stewardship is observation, shared-surface repair, mail, and escalation. Duty cycle runs on a schedule (owner-requested 2026-08-21); a cycle where nothing changed produces no owner traffic.
roles.trigger: Every scheduled duty cycle; immediately when a Mac push, lane message, or sim-result lands; when a shared-surface change (run-live-lanes.sh, sim loop, harness) alters what the Mac must do.
roles.produced: PR #223 aftercare: lane mail with re-run instructions, ack of the Mac's harness message, standing 4-hour monitor routine
roles.nextAction: The Fleet trial expires September 16, 2026 and the Mac lane holds the only enrollable device, so the seven unverified endpoint dimensions have a deadline this lane cannot move. Confirm the queued sim-requests are drained and report the remaining debt to the owner while the trial is still live.
